en: Solid carbon dioxide, called dry ice, does not melt into a liquid but sublimates directly into a gas at room temperature.
Oobleck is a non-Newtonian fluid made of cornstarch and water that acts like a solid when punched but flows like a liquid when poured.
Gallium is a solid metal at room temperature, but it will melt into a liquid puddle just from the natural heat of your bare hand.
Aerogel is a solid material made mostly of trapped air, making it so light that a brick-sized piece can balance on a delicate flower.
Honey is a supersaturated sugar solution containing more dissolved sugar than water can normally hold, which is why it eventually crystallizes into solid grains.
Red cabbage juice acts as a natural chemical indicator, turning bright pink in acidic vinegar and bluish-green in basic baking soda solutions.
Milk is an emulsion, a specific type of mixture where tiny, invisible droplets of liquid fat are permanently suspended throughout a liquid water base.
Pure distilled water is actually an electrical insulator that does not conduct electricity, but dissolved salts in tap water make it a conductor.
Lightning is a superheated plasma, which is a fourth state of matter where gases become so hot that their electrons separate from their atoms.
Liquid nitrogen is so incredibly cold at minus 196 degrees Celsius that it instantly freezes a room-temperature flower into a solid, glass-like state.
When you mix warm milk and vinegar, a chemical change occurs that clumps the liquid proteins together into solid curds to make simple plastic.
A water strider insect can walk on a pond because water's high surface tension creates an invisible, elastic-like skin strong enough to support its weight.
